ChangeGroups.Name: Changes
Changes: The mod's log holds a line or two per city load instead of about 10 KB of diagnostics, and the game's own log no longer gets warnings from it that a player could not act on.

ChangeGroups.Name: Changes
Changes: Each menu's tabs follow the game's own tab row, the menu picker follows the toolbar, and the All tab's headings follow the tabs.
Development tree tabs and headings use the game's own names, in the game's language, instead of English.
Education's school tabs and school-tier headings name each level after the game's own school, in the game's language.

Subcategory headings and labels, the All tab and chip, and theme names use the game's own words, in the game's language. In English, Paths reads Pathways, Shrubs & Bushes reads Bushes, and Extractor Zones reads Specialized Industry.
The Role filter and role headings use the game's name for each role, in the game's language.
An asset that several development tree nodes unlock is filed under one of them by a rule modelled on how the game unlocks it, instead of whichever came first.
Changing or clearing a filter or a range starts the list again at its first 100 rows.
The footer's counts group their digits the way the game does.
Replace the vanilla build menu takes effect at once, without a restart. Turning it off hands an open menu back to the game.

ChangeGroups.Name: Asset details
Changes: Hovering an asset shows more of the game's own tooltip: pollution levels, a power plant's voltage, power line capacity on roads, transformer capacity, input and output, water pipes on roads, and transport stops. A network's cost includes its auxiliary networks. Most lines use the game's wording, in every language it ships.
An incinerator's Capacity is its garbage store, and its electricity gets a Power output line.
Power output adds up every source a building has instead of showing only the largest.
Zoned and signature buildings show no upkeep figure, as in the game's tooltip. The table's Upkeep column, sort and range skip them.
Upgrades read as the game reads them: Resource consumption -20 %, pollution changes as signed percentages, and graduation as +5 %.
Negative wellbeing, health and work conditions are shown with their sign.
Cemetery and crematorium capacity is a plain number, as in the game's tooltip.
Comfort is shown for parking and transport stops, a geothermal plant says it needs ground water, and a hydroelectric dam shows its own cost and upkeep.
Effects use the game's units, a shelter's vehicles read Evacuation buses, homes per cell keep a decimal, a road with no upkeep has no upkeep line, and deathcare processing rounds up.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: With a menu open, clicking a building on the map shows its info panel.
After a search, Enter picks the best match you can place, in every view.
A trailing space in the search box no longer loses matches.
With a tab selected, the number of matches elsewhere is what Search everything finds.
Typing in a filter's own search box no longer breaks the panel.
The resize edge stays under the cursor while dragging, at every resolution.
Load more says how many rows it adds, and a double click loads once.
The metric filter's badge counts the ranges set.
The category chip's picker offers only the tabs shown.
The Small Roads tab and heading no longer carry a stray line break.
The Content filter's icon is drawn.
The reverse-sort button's tooltip reads Reverse sort.
The Options screen shows its labels in English in the 13 languages that had none translated.
On a Turkish system, words such as Industrial are capitalised correctly.
If the panel fails while drawing, the game's own menu, upgrades picker or tool options take its place. If indexing fails, the panel keeps the city's last complete index.
With the upgrades picker open, the mouse wheel zooms and extensions can be placed above it.
A filter row with two icons keeps them on one line at every resolution.
Search everything shows its whole label at 1280x720.
Very long names are shortened in the middle in the list and card views.

ChangeGroups.Name: Compatibility
Changes: Road Builder: an edited road is replaced in its menu and tab at once, numbered duplicates keep their numbers, and discarded roads no longer appear on a session's first load.
Find It: an asset whose tag names a category pair the panel does not have is listed under its own category instead of being dropped.
Asset UI Manager and other mods that move a category or an asset between menus: it gets one heading in the All tab, in its place.

ChangeGroups.Name: Performance
Changes: Typing a search or dragging the resize edge no longer redraws every row.
The mod no longer copies every object and road in the city once a minute.
A full index pass no longer checks each building's mesh against every other's, and building or bulldozing a unique building no longer refreshes a closed panel.

ChangeGroups.Name: Changes
Changes: The panel's drag-to-resize edge shows the game's own resize cursor on hover and while dragging, and its grip is drawn at the weight of the game's scrollbar thumb, so the edge reads as something to grab. Hovering it showed no cursor at all before.
The panel can be dragged down to a single row of cards; before, it stopped at about four rows.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: In Grid view, a category with room for its tiles in one row no longer stacks some of them into a column; in Cards view the same rows sit a hair tighter. Both were the same rounding error in how the panel spaced a row.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: Mods that add their own text no longer each cause a full re-index while the game loads. The index is rebuilt once after the last of them, so a large playset loads without the seconds of stutter per mod.
The Already Built mark on unique buildings and upgrades is drawn at the size of the picture again. Game version 1.6.2 stopped stretching it, so it covered the whole card.
The Upgrades panel has the same drag-to-resize edge as the build menu. Dragging either sets the height for both; a panel with few rows stays short.

In Cards view, a category whose cards wrap onto a second row no longer stretches the first row's cards to double height and hides the ones that wrapped; every card the heading counts is drawn, and a row of cards that fits the category's width stays on one line.

ChangeGroups.Name: Compatibility
Changes: Anarchy's "place multiple unique buildings" option now works through this panel. Whether an asset counts as already built is asked of the game per asset, so any mod that changes that answer changes ours.

ChangeGroups.Name: Compatibility
Changes: Buttons other mods add to the game's asset category tab bar now have a home in the panel. Zone Color Changer's "Edit Zone Colors" button appears while a zone is selected, as it does in the vanilla menu.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: A category another mod adds at runtime now draws its own icon in the tab strip instead of a blank placeholder.

ChangeGroups.Name: Compatibility
Changes: Menus the mod cannot fill are handed back to the vanilla grid instead of drawing an empty panel. Extra Assets Importer's menu, built from ExtraLib's nested categories, now shows its decals, lanes and surfaces as before.
Anything the vanilla menu places is indexed even when its prefab type is unknown to the mod. Water Features' ten water tools now appear under Landscaping.
An asset's category follows the game's live placement, so mods that regroup the menus at runtime (Asset UI Manager, Zone Organizer) show their tabs in the panel.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: When the game adds a newly subscribed copy of the mod to a session that is already loading a city, the mod's usual indexing hook has already passed and the index was built only when loading finished. The mod now indexes on its first update when it joins a running city, so the menu is ready as soon as the loading screen lifts.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: Subscribing to the mod and loading a city in the same session left the game with a blank white screen. The mod's hook around the game's tool options panel added a React hook to a panel that was already on screen, so the panel's next render threw. The wrapper no longer adds a hook; a separate wrapper re-renders the panel when the menu changes hands. Asset Menu Tweaks was not involved; the two mods were tested together in both load orders and work.

ChangeGroups.Name: Changes
Changes: Removed the "Show coverage map while placing" option. The game switches to a service's coverage view on its own whenever one of its buildings is on the tool; the option changed nothing.
Removed the "Select the first asset when opening the building menu" option. It had no effect.
Removed the "Hide Random asset types" option. The Random rock, boulder and trash pile in Landscaping are listed like everything else.
Removed the empty Key-Bindings tab from the mod's options page.
Reworded the "Searching widens automatically" description.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: The "Replace the vanilla build menu" option said Roads and Landscaping were unaffected. They are replaced like every other menu; the option text now says so.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: Expanded table rows: a figure's label no longer wraps under its value and spills into the placement chips; each label and value moves to the next line as a pair.
Expanded table rows no longer show "DLC -2009" on base-game assets; that number is the game's own base-game marker, and the Source line already says where the asset comes from.

ChangeGroups.Name: Fixes
Changes: The expand arrow at the end of each Table row drew as a missing-character box; it is now the game's own arrow glyph.

ChangeGroups.Name: Changes
Changes: First release on Paradox Mods.
A building browser inside every vanilla build menu: table, grid and card views with sorting, grouping and search.
Facets (availability, source, theme, asset pack, placement, role) and metric range filters (cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot size).
Hover cards with the figures the simulation reads, in either unit system.
Coverage overlay while placing a service building.
Named rows with cost and footprint in the extension picker.
Derived from Find It 1.5.8; the object picker and detailing features are not carried over.
